articleTitle: A parallel processing technique for a prime factor algorithm
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Proposes an engine dependent prime factor algorithm for the computation of an N-point discrete Fourier transform in real-time, where N is prime. A mathematical model for the algorithm is derived and simulation is carried out using Fortran code. The engine modelled is based on commercially available digital signal microprocessors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The effect of solid state power amplifiers (SSPAs) nonlinearities on MPSK and M-QAM signal transmission
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Simple four-parameter formulas model are presented for solid state power amplifiers (SSPAs) exhibiting both amplitude nonlinearity (AM/AM) and amplitude modulation to phase modulation conversion (AM/PM). Based on these models closed form expressions of symbol error probability for M-PSK and M-QAM signals transmitted through nonlinear SSPA in the presence of white additive Gaussian noise for a terrestrial link with a coherent receiver are calculated. Also the optimum values for the decision threshold levels and phase shift are calculated in order to minimise the error probability. The effect of SSPA input back off from the saturation point on M-QAM and M-PSK system performance are studied.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Time-frequency representation of linear time-varying systems using the Weyl symbol
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: The Weyl symbol (WS) representation of linear operators is introduced for the time-frequency analysis of linear time-varying systems. The authors show that, from a joint time-frequency point of view, the WS and the usual time-varying transfer function (ZF) as introduced by Zadeh (1950) have similar theoretical justification. Interpretation, estimation, properties, and relations of both the WS and the usual ZF are elaborated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The transmission of digital television in the UHF band using orthogonal frequency division multiplexing
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: As a result of work on digital television being conducted under contract to the Independent Television Commission (ITC), National Transcommunications Ltd., (NTL) has been able to demonstrate that it is technically feasible to transmit digital television in UHF channels which are at present unused. This is made possible by the marriage of two techniques, both of which make extensive use of digital signal processing. The first of these is the use of picture coding algorithms, which allow very high quality pictures to be reproduced for transmission at bit rates as low as 12 Mbit/second. The second, which the paper is concerned with, is orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), which as well as being a very robust means of transmitting data, also has excellent interference rejection properties.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An improved high precision formant analysis procedure
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Describes an improved method and it's implementation for the extraction of formants from high order autoregressive models, using previously described techniques. Test results are presented for synthetic and real data and it is shown that success rates of over 80% are now obtainable for model orders as high as 200. The procedure described will find the factors of a polynomial using signal processing techniques rather than numerical methods, which are unreliable for such high order models. The algorithm accepts an LPC model of a sample of a drum beat, found by any conventional method, for analysis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Nonlinear adaptive equalisation (multilayer perceptron)
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Develops the concept of the linear equaliser as a classification process within the domain of digital communications equalisation. From this point it is demonstrated that nonlinear adaptive structures are in fact more suited to solving this classification problem. The result of applying this concept is illustrated by developing a very general nonlinear adaptive structure in the form of the multilayer perceptron. Simple examples are provided which clearly illustrate the advantageous performance compared to linear equivalents.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and implementation of cascaded allpass digital filter structures with magnitude and delay constraints
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Considers a filter structure made up from a parallel arrangement of two allpass subfilters. Such structures were used originally in multi-rate problems but have also been applied to conventional filtering. The authors examine the design process and look at approaches using single-line and dual-line templates, the latter being used in conjunction with simulated annealing which gives a finite wordlength solution directly. Furthermore, they describe how this structure can be modified to cope with bandpass and multiple bandpass requirements. Hardware implementation is briefly discussed too and the paper concludes with some design examples illustrating the two methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Text-independent speaker recognition based on vowel spotting
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: An automatic text-independent speaker recognition system is presented, which is suitable for identification as well as for verification purposes. The system is based on spotting the stable part of the vowel phonemes of the test utterances, extracting parameter vectors and classifying them to a speaker-dependent vowel reference database. The system was tested over a period of four months with a population of 12 male and female speakers with non-correlated training and test data. The accuracy of the system as measured by experimentation is satisfactory considering that the training utterances per speaker do not exceed 50 sec and the test utterances 1 sec in average.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A comparison of acoustic noise cancellation techniques for telephone speech
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: With an ever increasing emphasis on improving communication systems, a significant amount of research has been put into digital speech coding and transmission systems. Lagging somewhat behind is a detailed approach to the analysis and removal of external acoustic interference from the pre-coded speech signal. The successful operation of telephone networks depends on the provision of coding economy with a required recovered speech signal quality, frequently under arduous input acoustic conditions. the paper evaluates the effectiveness of several acoustic noise cancellation techniques when applied in the telephone kiosk environment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Off-line cursive-script recognition using a neural network
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Reports the applications of a feed-forward neural network classifier to a cursive-script recognition system. One of the difficulties of cursive-script recognition is the variability of styles of writers. Having this problem in mind and knowing the widely recognised ability of neural networks to generalise, the authors developed a cursive-script recognition system which takes a normalised geometrical features as inputs, and the outputs correspond to any letter of the English lower-case alphabet. The results for single and two writers are encouraging.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance of sequential detection schemes for trellis-encoded data signals distorted by intersymbol interference
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: The authors propose the use of a sequential detection scheme for the combined equaliser/decoder trellis. They deal with the generalised stack algorithm (GSA). They investigate the GSA for trellis coded modulation data signals and compare it with the reduced state sequence estimator (RSSE) method. For the simulations, Ungerboeck codes were used. The aim of the study was to examine data transmission over typical band limited telephone channels having passband responses between 300 and 3400 Hz.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A trellis-coded 2.048 MB/s data transmission system for ISDN
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: The two major impairments in high rate digital subscriber loop (HDSL) transmission are severe intersymbol interference (ISI) and the near-end crosstalk (NEXT). At the primary rate (2.048 MB/s) the problem becomes even worse because the impulse response of the channel stretches over many symbol intervals and the NEXT noise increases with frequency. The authors use a double side (both pre- and postcursor) fractionally spaced (T/2) forward filter (FSFF) to suppress the NEXT noise in the detector. The double side FSFF cancels the precursor ISI as well. The postcursor part of the ISI will either be canceled by a decision feedback equalizer (DFE) or be used by a maximum likelihood detector. They propose a trellis-coded 8PAM for 2.048 Mb/s data transmission on the DSL channel using the reduced state sequence estimation (RSSE) or the sequential sequence estimation (SSE) method. This system is compared with an uncoded 4PAM (called 2B1Q) system in which the DFE is used to eliminate the IS of the channel.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development and implementation of an adaptive digital beamforming network for satellite communication systems
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Recent advances in digital technology, have enabled the design of single chip digital beamforming networks. This, coupled with advances in digital signal processor technology, enables complete beamforming systems to be constructed at a lower cost, thus making the application of these techniques to commercial communications systems attractive. The authors describe the design and development of such an adaptive digital beamforming network by ERA Technology for the European Space Agency. The system is being developed as a proof of concept laboratory-based demonstrator to enable the feasibility of adaptive digital beamforming techniques for communication systems to be determined. Ultimately, digital beamforming could be used in conjunction with large array antennas for communication satellite systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Discrete-time domain poles zeros identification using back propagation neural networks
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Describes a back propagation neural network applying to poles zeros identification in discrete time domain. Traditional recursive least squares (RLS) algorithm is time consuming and sensitive to noise. Neural networks possess massive parallel processing capability and noise immunity, the time and noise constraints can be eliminated. The results are encouraging and demonstrate that neural networks offer new promising directions towards solving system identification problems radically.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fractal coding of still images
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Reviews the basic principles of the construction of fractal objects with iterated function systems, and explains how such a technique has been adopted by Jacquin (1989) for the coding (compression) of digital images. New methods are also proposed for the enhancement of Jacquin's approach, and the significance of using these methods is discussed in terms of processing time and the quality of the coded images.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of the binary Hough transform to image compression
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Presents the application of the binary Hough transform to compression/decompression of line drawings and multiple gray level images. The performance of the proposed technique is evaluated for some examples.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Study of the first-order curvature of array manifold for spherical-wave propagation
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Superresolution array processing an in particular signal subspace-type techniques are based effectively on the searching of the array manifold in order to estimate signal parameter. The differential geometry of the manifold of a general array of isotropic sensors receiving signals from near-field sources was investigated. Expressions for the rate of change of manifold arc length and first curvature as a function of source bearing and range were presented and their behaviour was discussed for the special case of a uniform linear array. It was thereby shown that the shape of the azimuth ( theta -parameter) curves deviates from that of a hyperhelix for decreasing values of range.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An interactive tool for segmentation and acoustic-phonetic analysis of speech SPANEX
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: The SPANEX software has been developed for the extraction of phonetic patterns from different corpuses. It provides a means of editing and analysing speech signals. The objective of this software is to increase the efficiency of acoustic-phonetic analysis of speech. Using this tool one can record and play back sentences, compute, display, and analyse spectrograms or pitch contours as well as perform the labelling of speech utterances. Moreover, coarticulation phenomena can be studied, the voiced/unvoiced error can be edited graphically and submitted to a smoothing procedure. Each speech segment may be zoomed in context, displayed and examined. Hence, SPANEX is an efficient and easy-to-use tool for the development of algorithms in speech recognition and synthesis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A fractal-based source model for ATM packet video (video codec)
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: A fractal-based traffic source is proposed, as an accurate model for the the 'bursty', low bit-rate traffic produced by a typical VBR video coding scheme. The model is based on a switched-fractal algorithm, which switches between five constant-activity, fractal-based, cell generation modes, in a normally-distributed manner, in an attempt to reproduce the low-level, cell-generation process. The accuracy of this model (which has been verified by comparing the traffic produced by this source with 'real' traffic, produced through the simulated compression of two test images), combined with its simple implementation, makes it an ideal source model for highly compressed, variable bit-rate packet video.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Classification of shape for content retrieval of images in a multimedia database
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Presents a powerful and general procedure for the parametric classification of image 'objects'. The parameters used are related to general 'shape' properties, but the technique can very easily be extended to other perceptually significant sets of parameters related to texture, colour, size, etc. Furthermore, the representation is such that queries can be constructed from iconic class representations, example images or even example sketches. Five perceptually meaningful shape parameters are used. These are the 'circularity', 'transparency', 'aspect ratio', 'irregularity' and the 'extreme point ratio'. The values of these parameters, for a particular 'object', form a vector which represents a point in 'shape' space. The classification is performed by identifying clusters of points in this space during a training phase. Since the training data is spread over a continuum and the number of classes within the data is unknown prior to training it is appropriate to use an unsupervised classification technique.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation of packet-based encoding schemes for speech transmission
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Missing packets due to network congestion can seriously degrade the quality of received speech in voice packet communication. The natural redundancy of speech offers some protection against loss and about 1 to 2% missing packets cause little noticeable distortion if silence is substituted for the missing segments. The implementation of packet-based embedded coding (PBEC) and the performance of a simple encoder/decoder which exploits PBEC are discussed. The encoder/decoder combines the sample-by-sample predictive mode necessary for low bit rate operation with whole packet prediction for missing packet reconstruction.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive receiver structures with sequential detection algorithms for digital mobile radio systems
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: The maximum likelihood sequence estimation (MLSE) represents the optimum detection process. It is effectively realizable by the Viterbi algorithm (VA). Suboptimum sequential detection algorithms (SDA) observe only a limited number of paths, which results in a complexity reduction but also to a degradation against the VA. Adaptive receiver structures including three different SDA are presented: the M-algorithm, stack algorithm and the generalised stack algorithm. All three are sorting algorithms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A high speed RSA processor
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: With the explosion of electronic data communications and computer networks, it has become important to develop new ways to guarantee their security. Two techniques are available: the private key system (e.g. DES), and the public key systems (e.g. RSA). The private key systems are more widely used than the public key systems because they are fast and easy to implement, but they suffer from serious disadvantages such as lower security and complexity in distribution of the key. Public key systems provide much higher security levels and no need for key distribution. However, their use has been limited to key distribution for the private key systems because they are very slow. The paper describes three techniques for increasing the speed of the central computational process in the RSA algorithm, i.e. modular exponentiation. Together they achieve a speed improvement of about 7 to 1.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementing a digital video codec in hardware for real-time bit-rate reduction of television images
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: The authors outline the SPECTRE coding algorithm which achieves the required data compression whilst maintaining broadcast quality. It is based on the hybrid discrete cosine transform (DCT) coding scheme, with motion compensated prediction. It also uses an advanced interpolative prediction technique, employing information from both previous and next frames. The algorithm has been optimised in simulations to operate at 12 Mbit/s, but in principle other bit rates are possible for different applications. Furthermore, it can dynamically adjust to changes in picture content, allocating any spare capacity in the video stream during periods of low picture activity to additional data services.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new class of analysis by synthesis LPC coders: multipulse excited sunbed LPC
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: A new class of analysis by synthesis LPC algorithms, called multipulse excited subband (MESB), is presented. The proposed system differs from the conventional analysis by synthesis LPC systems in that the excitation sequence is defined by a sparse sequence of pulses in each subband. The pulses in each subband are determined by a closed loop optimization procedure similar to the multipulse excited linear predictive coding (MELPC). Since the excitation is split into different subbands, the sampling rate of the pulses in each subband is reduced to its corresponding Nyquist rate. The combinations of pulse positions in each subband are thus substantially diminished and hence the positional coding bit rates are reduced. Furthermore the system employs a closed-loop optimization procedure which evades aliasing distortion and interband leakage introduced by the imperfection of the filters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design and implementation of lattice codes using digital signal processing techniques
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Addresses the design of lattice coding systems with the potential for both significant coding gain and very high speed operation, without impractical complexity. The conventional approach to the implementation of advanced modulation and coding schemes has been to employ general purpose programmable DSP chips. This limits the speed of operation to a few tens of kb/s at most, which has restricted the use of these schemes to applications such as voiceband modems. However, if the designer makes appropriate choices of lattice and algorithm it is possible to construct dedicated hardware, perhaps implemented in ASIC, capable of running at tens of hundreds of Mb/s. Two families of lattice which are suitable for hardware implementation are described. A suitable decoding algorithm is presented together with the resulting architecture.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel subband DCT image coding
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: In transform image coding an image is usually divided into subimages before processing. Though a smaller size subimage is efficient for computation, it introduces blocking effect. However, an increase in subimage size results in an increase in both storage and computational requirements. The authors propose an efficient coding approach to simulate a full-size DCT image coding with subband decomposition technique in such a way that only a small increase in storage is required. Compared with the conventional DCT transform coding, this coding technique has the advantages of no blocking effect; higher quality reconstructed images; and less computational effort required.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A parallel multidimensional digital signal processing technique
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: A parallel processing technique for multidimensional linear time invariant (LTI) systems is proposed. The resultant structures are regular, modular and highly parallelism. The approach used is systematic therefore, it would be useful for logic synthesis. The application of this approach in DSP and numerical computations reduces the design time which results in low design cost. this approach produces various structures (semi-systolic, quasi-systolic and pure systolic arrays) which could be considered as application specific array processors. The parallel algorithm described is used for mapping multidimensional DSP onto VLSI, ULSI and WSI array structures. The technique is used to design 2-D digital filters and parallel DFT structures for image processing applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Traffic control parameters for video sources in ATM networks (video codec simulation)
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Describes a study of video traffic behaviour in ATM networks with respect to the choice of values for policing function and call acceptance control parameters. Results are presented based on traffic obtained through the simulation of a typical conditional replenishment video codec. By looking at the maximum virtual cell rate of multiplexed traffic, using a sampling interval determined by the capacity of the ATM buffer, the ideal statistical multiplexing gain over a link is shown. A traffic control system based on a linear call acceptance control algorithm and the policing of the virtual mean and virtual peak cell rates using moving windows are discussed. It is shown that the independent policing of the sources restricts the achievement of the multiplexing gain initially demonstrated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An experiment in multimedia communication for gynaecology
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: It is important for medical consultants at different sites to share information, such as microscope images, about which they are discussing. The authors describe work carried out to provide multimedia communication facilities for two gynaecologists in different hospitals. The communication system configuration is shown. Communicating sites are connected by ISDN30 and MATMX (Model ATM Exchange) provides an ATM interface for application components. The operation of the video transmitter and receiver and the voice codec is controlled via a user interface on the Unix workstation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer simulation of the output of a variable bit rate video codec
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Addresses the analysis and subsequent simulation of a video codec producing a variable bit rate output. The work is directed towards two areas, namely line-by-line characteristics within a frame, and frame-by-frame statistics within a video sequence. This allows the appropriate degree of resolution to be incorporated within a simulation model. Initially, statistics from a real video source representing 'head and shoulders' viewphone type pictures were obtained, and coded by a commercial, COST 211 codec. These were then analysed to find a common statistical distribution representing each set. The distributions were then used as a basis for the simulation models.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An efficient multidimensional/multidirectional parallel pipelined architecture for image processing
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: The architecture of a multidimensional and multidirectional parallel pipeline system is presented. It is based on the concept of algorithm-to-architecture mapping whereby different stages of the pipeline can be dynamically reconfigured to suit different task divisions in terms of processing power or memory required. The system has a high degree of fault tolerance provided by the multiple interconnection links among the processing elements within each stage and between different stages. An 8-PEs prototype version of the system has been built and tested under various configurations of pipeline stages. A combination of various algorithms have been implemented on the system and predicted results are obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Digital block phase and frequency offset estimation in burst mode MSK transmission
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Acquisition of burst mode packetised data over a satellite channel involves frequency offset estimation and block phase estimation for coherent demodulation of data. The paper describes a non-decision directed, asynchronous block phase estimator for use in demodulation of baseband MSK in-phase and quadrature (I&Q) signals for AWGN channels. Automatic frequency compensation (at intermediate frequency) through a control voltage to a VCXO is provided using LMS parameter estimation on the carrier recovery bits present in the preamble of every burst. The MSK-burst modems have been implemented in real time at 16 kbps using a TMS320C30 based DSP board.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: DPCM video signal/image Fourier transform
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: A novel approach is proposed to increase the throughput rate and reduce the hardware cost requirement of the linear systolic matrix-vector multiplication architecture for 2D Fourier transform implementation. This is achieved by coding video signal/images more efficiently using 6-bit 1D DPCM coding system prior to processing. It is shown that using 6-bit DPCM processing results in 64% improvement in speed and a significant saving in the hardware cost. The effect of quantisation errors on DPCM video signal/image Fourier transforms is also presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High speed object recognition system
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: A high speed object recognition system is designed and developed for recognizing a set of handtools. The system is not only capable of handling the scaling and orientation problems, but also can recognize partially occluded objects. Corners and curves which are detected based on different order of discontinuities are selected as the primitive local features of an object. After feature detection, a back propagation network (BP net) is employed as a classifier. A set of general handtools is selected to evaluate the performance of the system and the results are encouraging. The recognition time is less than 6 seconds with an IBM AT computer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel pulse-excitation using coded locations for linear predictive speech coding
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: The authors propose a new excitation model which can produce high quality speech at low bit rate (8 kbit/s) with low computational complexity. The excitation is represented by a sequence of pulses whose locations are coded by a small random codebook, and their corresponding amplitudes are solved such that the perceptual error between original and synthetic speech is minimized. They discover that the size of the codebook for the pulse locations can be made practically small without severe degradation. In order to further increase the quality of the speech, another source of excitation can be added. This excitation is obtained from a very small white Gaussian noise codebook so as to compensate the perceptual error between the original speech and the synthetic speech of the first excitation source. Since both codebooks are small in size, this scheme can be implemented with a low cost digital signal processor such as TMS320C25.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of multi-rate sampling techniques in a satellite communications link simulator
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: British Aerospace (Space Systems) has developed a satellite communications system software simulator which makes extensive use of multi-rate digital signal processing techniques to improve computational efficiency. The simulator model includes the network of ground terminals, the satellite antennas and satellite transponder channel, together with signal generators which explicitly model each user link (called accesses) as transmitted from the ground terminals. Uplink and downlink noise and interference sources are also modelled. The simulator is used to evaluate the performance of digital satellite communications links and applications include FDMA (frequency division multiple access) planning, analysis of spread spectrum systems, power spectrum analysis and performance measurement of individual accesses. The paper describes two of the more important multi-rate structures in the software, namely the signal generator modules and the uplink multiplexer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Architectural considerations for adaptive digital signal processing within long-range radio communications system terminals
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: The proposed 'generic', or flexible radio system architecture comprises of the transceiver unit which handles the interface of the base-band data to the communications medium, and the controller unit, realised by a computer integrated with DSP devices. Since the transceiver units are commercially available the only requisite for this type of terminal architecture is the availability of a remote control and audio interface. The DSP device perform all of the dedicated signal processing operations, such as adaptive modem implementation, error control coding and real-time channel evaluation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance of rate selective punctured convolutional codes of equal code length
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: A family of (PC) codes of rate v/N is presented, where N is constant and even and v can be varied between N/2 and (N-1). These PC codes are called rate selective punctured convolutional codes of equal code length (RSPC codes). From best known rate 1/2 codes, a set of good RSPC codes of rates 7/12 to 11/12 having memory 2<=M<=6 have been derived, and the maximum free distance d/sub f/ and minimum information weight C(d/sub f/) of these RSPC codes are provided. The RSPC coding/Viterbi decoding scheme with soft decision has been simulated. The obtained bit error rate (BER) performances with rates 7/12 to 11/12 for a Gaussian channel are provided.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A high-quality 8 kbps multi-pulse coder using a single TMS320C25
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: A real-time implementation of an 8 kbps high-quality multi-pulse coder on a single chip DSP is given. The coder employs a new multi-pulse analysis structure which allows a fast algorithm to be used for calculating the cross-correlation between the input speech and the impulse response of the LPC filter. A fast algorithm for searching the pulse information is given. A simple and fast coding scheme for packing the pulse positions to low data rates is also addressed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Orthogonal decomposition on the backward prediction errors for faster glottal inverse filtering
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Glottal inverse filtering (GIF) could be considered as a step forward in human voice modelling through parametrical analysis. The paper begins with a geometrical approach of the GIF problem, directly derived from the linear prediction framework. The most recently proposed algorithm is then reviewed, with a special emphasis on its geometrical interpretation as a decomposition process in a vector space. The authors then introduce a somewhat modified and more efficient algorithm based on orthogonal decomposition on the well-known backward prediction error vectors, and give raw experimental results and further research directions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive subspace image vector quantization and its relationship with transform coding using VQ
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Novel complexity reduction methods for spatial domain image vector quantization based on subspace distortion is proposed. Substantial reductions in computation and memory requirement are obtained while maintaining good image quality. Experimental results show that the fixed-basis subspace distortion method can achieve as much as four times improvement in both computation speed and memory requirement with an image quality degradation of not more than 0.4 dB in peak signal to noise ratio for many real images, The adaptive-basis subspace distortion method can achieve almost 16 times complexity reduction for the case of binary tree-searched VQ. It has further been shown that the proposed subspace VQ method is always better than a corresponding transform domain VQ having the same complexity. The proposed methods are general and can be applied in combination with many other image VQ techniques to achieve further improvements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Pole-zero code excited linear prediction
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: A new speech coding algorithm 'pole-zero CELP' is proposed in which the short-time spectral envelope of the speech wave is modelled with a pole-zero filter. Objective and subjective comparisons of a CELP (12 pole and 14 pole) and a pole-zero CELP (8 pole-6 zero and 12 pole-6 zero) coder are made. The results presented show that pole-zero CELP is able to reproduce the original speech signal better than the CELP coder. The informal subjective tests show a preference for the pole-zero CELP coder (12 pole-6 zero).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Self-orthogonal codes constructed from cyclic squares
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Self-orthogonal codes are a class of one-step majority logic decodable (MLD) codes; i.e. they have a very simple decoding algorithm and relatively low cost, although performance is below the theoretical limits of some codes with similar rate and minimum distances. The ideas of cyclic square and complete set of cyclic squares, and some operations on them, are introduced. From these one can easily construct a class of self-orthogonal codes. This kind of codes has the virtue of being adjustable in its error control capacities, and a strong potential to be employed in communication and information storage systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A modified Orwell protocol for VBR video
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: An integrated services protocol called Orwell-B is presented. It is a modification of the Orwell protocol, a distributed control protocol that eliminates the need for a monitor node. The protocol supports all the features of the original Orwell protocol and introduces the concept of surplus cells which reduce queuing delays of low priority traffic at the same time increasing the throughput of the network at low and medium loads. Studies of network simulations are presented, illustrating the advantages of the modified protocol.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Parallel processing of digital images using a modular architecture
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Describes a parallel modular architecture that can perform high speed image processing by implementing digital signal processing algorithms in hardware. Speed performance is enhanced by the fact that different modules can be working simultaneously in parallel, on the same or a different set of data. The authors look in detail at how one of the parallel modules operates, and they propose how the system can be used to compress the data required to send or store a sequence of image frames, by encoding changes in consecutive frames in terms of geometric transformations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Two dimensional dilation correlation functions
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: A development of the cross/auto correlation function is discussed which is capable of detecting and quantifying stretching or contraction between functions in two or more dimensions. Some properties of this function are discussed and a range of illustrations are examined. One of these concerns an application to the detection of thermal expansion effects on images of combustion in internal combustion engines.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Real time videophone image coding algorithm simulation on a concurrent supercomputer
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: A flexible means of evaluating/developing videophone image compression algorithms is required. Here we analyse their mapping and contrast it with currently popular alternative ones. Additional results are presented for speed up, efficiency and absolute simulation speeds achieved.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fast vector quantisation using orthogonal codebooks
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Vector quantisation techniques are commonly used in the digital transmission of analogue signals such as voice and images. For examples, speech coding using CELP (code excited linear prediction) has already found application in communication systems where high speech quality is required at low bit rates. The paper addresses one of the drawbacks of CELP as originally proposed by Atal and Schroeder (1984) which is its high computational complexity. The authors propose an approach called FVQ-CELP fast vector quantisation CELP which typically reduces the computational load by more than two orders of magnitude compared with conventional schemes, while maintaining high speech quality.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An evaluation of spectral transitivity functions for speech segmentation in variable frame rate LPC synthesis
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Three different formulations of spectral transitivity function based on LPC derived coefficients are evaluated for speech segmentation in a variable frame rate (VFR) vocoder. The quality of VFR vocoded speech has been compared with that of a fixed frame rate vocoder and some suggestions are made for further improvements to the segmentation, on the basis of this comparison.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: MAP estimation in image restoration by a local search enhanced genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Investigates a maximum a posteriori distribution (MAP) estimation approach to image restoration. Images are modelled as Markov random fields (MRF), a form of 2-D stochastic process. The authors present a new MAP estimation algorithm which combines a global search method, the genetic algorithm (GA), and a fast local search strategy, iterated conditional modes (ICM). This hybrid algorithm combines the fast convergence of ICM with the power of sustained exploration from the GA in order to achieve a good optimum, if not the global one. the major modification to the GA is the introduction of local hill climbing and voting controlled mutation mechanisms. The algorithm is used to restore two artificial images, both distorted by an independent additive Gaussian noise. The results are compared with that from ICM alone, and simulated annealing (SA). It is shown that the new MAP algorithm reaches a good optimum in a significantly smaller number of iterations compared with SA.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Singular value decomposition and its modelling of speech excitation
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: The desire to be able to design high quality low bit rate speech codecs has caused much recent research to be directed at the efficient representation of the excitation function information of the new established family of LPC codecs. The authors concentrate on the use of the singular value decomposition (SVD) procedure to construct an optimal orthogonal transformation domain in which the speech signal can be analysed. They consider the main characteristics and properties of the singular vectors of the LPC impulse response matrix that form the basis for the new SVD domain. Elementary coding approaches that seek to exploit the SVD domain properties are presented. A particular consideration is made of the characteristics and properties of the LPC excitation function in the transformation domain.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modelling and simulation of data transponding links for road-use debiting schemes
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: With the renewed interest in the development of short-range two-way data transponding links for possible use in road transport informatics schemes, computer modelling and simulations have become an invaluable tool for evaluating the performance of the systems. This paper describes a computer simulation architecture which models the transmitter/receiver operations at the transponder in a moving vehicle and at the interrogator at a stationary road-side beacon. The effects of transmission medium impairments and of the choice of system design parameters on the bit error rate performance of the link are evaluated by means of the simulation tool. The software package is modular, sufficiently flexible and user-friendly, and so is a tool which is especially suited for analysing a wide range of existing and potential short-range microwave data transponding links.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Combined coding modulation, carrier, and frame synchronization on the basis of time-variant coded 8/4-PSK
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: A frame synchronization is presented that is included in time-variant coded modulation without any loss in data rate. It delivers the phase offset to control the carrier loop. Time-variant coded modulation based on block codes is defined. There is no need for additional sync-headers. A detailed derivation of the corresponding probabilities to be out of sync has been included to simplify the selection of sync-sequences for a special application.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Estimation of rate of change of channel using fast start-up technique
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Deals with a fast start-up estimation of rate of change of channel based on a training signal consisting of a self-orthogonal sequence repeated several times. A process of maximum likelihood estimation of the sampled impulse response of the channel is carried out on the receipt of each linearly distorted self-orthogonal sequence (excluding the first sequence which acts as a buffer). For the correct operation of the system, the channel impulse response must not change significantly over the duration of any one self-orthogonal sequence. Results of extensive computer simulation tests are presented. A theoretical model of the channel is studied which incorporates the worst properties of both HF as well as mobile radio links, namely, frequency-selectivity and rapid fading rate.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer simulation of digital subscriber loop transceivers
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Modern digital subscriber loop transmission systems make use of adaptive digital signal processing techniques. The transceivers are designed to deal with the wide range of channel impairments encounted in the access network. It is important to fully simulate new algorithms and transmission methods before committing designs to hardware. The paper describes software modelling techniques that have resulted in simulation performance predictions to within 1 dB of measured hardware results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An LCA implementation of DSP functions
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Presents a case study for implementing digital signal processing functions using a programmable application specific IC. A logic cell array device is used to implement structures for sampling rate alteration. The denoted structures are well-suited for VLSI implementation because of their regularity and modularity. The performance and chip resources for an interpolator circuit are examined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Digital matched filters in unknown interference
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Examines the performance of digital matched filters with multi-level quantisation and dither in various type of impulsive interference. The work of Cahn (1971) is extended to eight quantisation level devices. It is then limited to binary quantisation steps to enable simple implementation using digital circuitry. Improvements to Cahn's device suggested by Turin (1976) are incorporated and the performance of the device evaluated in a variety of interference cases. The device is then further modified by a new suggestion, setting to zero inputs that are outside the region in which any information can be extracted. The performance of this new device is then discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A descent algorithm for L/sub 1/-deconvolution
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Presents a descent method for the minimisation of a functional that arises from the least absolute deviation problem. The method is aimed at ill-conditioned problems, i.e. problems where the columns of the matrix are not from linear dependence. In spite of the complications introduced for the sake of numerical stability, the procedure is fast and efficient.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Enhancement of coded speech signals using artificial neural network techniques
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Artificial neural network techniques have the capabilities of modelling both linear and nonlinear functions. It is believed that some sort of linear as well as nonlinear relationships do exist between a set of noisy signals and the corresponding clean signals and this can be exploited by using the neural network models. Therefore, the aim of the research work presented in the paper was to investigate the use of the artificial neural network techniques for the improvement of the quality of coded speech signals. The noise of primary concern here is the vector quantisation noise which has been added to the original speech samples during the coding process.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Spectral estimation of nonstationary time series
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: The spectral estimation of nonstationary time series is a long standing problem of major importance. Examples of such time series can be drawn from many diverse fields such a communications, foetal heart rate and condition monitoring. The time series involved can be nonstationary in mean, covariance or both. The authors examine a time series which is artificially generated and can have either a slowly or a rapidly changing spectrum. Attempts are made to model such time series using two different techniques so that their spectra may be estimated. The trade-offs involved in using the two different modelling techniques are then discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: DSP implementation of low bit-rate CELP based speech orders
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Low bit-rate speech coding techniques are very important in applications where power and bandwidth are very limited. Prime requirements for speech coding are low bit-rate, high quality and low implementation cost. Since 1984 CELP coding of speech has been most popular at medium to low bit-rates. The major drawback of CELP coding, however, has been its large computational requirement. The authors report on the real-time implementation of a CELP coder in a single DSP32C floating-point processor on a four-layer single Eurocard size board with its appropriate input/output stages and 32 kbytes of external RAM. They also report on various complexity reduction techniques that they have employed to achieve a single DSP solution for both encoder, decoder and a very effective voice activity detection (VAD) devices.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modelling the vocal tract using multiple digital signal processors
publicationTitle: 1991 Sixth International Conference on Digital Processing of Signals in Communications
abstract: Describes the experience obtained during the design, build and operation of a multiple digital signal processing system based on Texas Instruments TMS32020 chips. The system was designed specifically to explore the use of an electrical transmission line model representing the operation of the human vocal tract in which an utterance is defined by a set of parameters indicating the way in which the model is changing. The architecture adopted is that of a master 32020 communicating with (presently five) slave 32020s through shared global data memory. Each slave operates with local program memory (ROM and RAM) and the on-chip data RAM. The master communicates with a host personal computer through shared data and program memories.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
